When the server refuses a variable (its sshd has no matching AcceptEnv), type an export line for it into the new shell instead. The lines are visible on screen and in the shell history, values included — do not use this for secrets the server should hold only in the environment.
Acceptance means the server did not reject the request. Login profiles can still override a value — check in the shell if a command behaves unexpectedly.
Downloads for this host go straight into its local folder (see the host environment settings).
Tunnels run on their own connection, separate from the terminal session. Pick a host, configure its tunnels, jump chain, and proxy, then start them.
By default every tunnel binds to loopback (127.0.0.1) only, so it is reachable only from this device.
No hosts yet. Add a host first.
Allow non-loopback bind — exposes this port to the local network. Use only on trusted networks.
Delete the tunnel %1$s? Its configuration will be removed.
No jump hosts. Connections go directly to the target.
Remove all jump hosts for this host? The target host itself is not affected.
A SOCKS proxy operator can see the target hostname and port and the timing of the connection, though not the encrypted SSH content. Only use a proxy you trust.
No tunnels yet. Add one below.
Ports must be numbers between 1 and 65535.
sshj 0.40.0 has no SOCKS server, so there is nothing safe to offer here.
No standard-library support; a hand-written CONNECT handshake is unproven and is not shipped.
sshj has no ProxyCommand support, and bridging a local process to a socket is unproven here.
SOCKS authentication would need the JVM-global Authenticator, which would leak credentials across connections.

Remote desktop is conditional, not promised. RDP is blocked by the prompt 12 proof gate: no RDP connection has been demonstrated yet. VNC has a protocol core implemented but no session yet: it has never connected to a real VNC server. See the rows below for the exact state and what would unblock each.

Blocked by the prompt 12 proof-of-concept gate: no RDP connection has been demonstrated yet. FreeRDP is the only candidate, but it ships no Android library — its native code must be built from source with the Android NDK, and this environment has no NDK, no CI build, and no Windows endpoint to test against.

Candidate: FreeRDP 3.x, actively maintained, with an Android port updated in recent releases. Its core is Apache-2.0; the full licence inventory for the exact linked components is still open and must come from the FreeRDP source tree at integration time.

What would unblock it: a CI machine with the NDK that builds the FreeRDP native libraries for the target ABIs, a licence inventory for the exact linked components, and a real connection to a compatible Windows endpoint — Pro, Enterprise, or Education with Remote Desktop enabled. Windows Home cannot host a Remote Desktop session.

Protocol core implemented, session not yet available: a pure-Kotlin RFB client core is in the app — protocol versions 3.3, 3.7 and 3.8, No Authentication and VNC Authentication, and Raw, CopyRect, RRE, CoRRE and Hextile framebuffer decoding — with unit tests for the protocol logic. It has never connected to a real VNC server.

Blocked by the prompt 13 proof-of-concept gate for a session: the pack requires a proven connection against a controlled compatible server before full integration, and this environment has no controlled Linux VNC server, no device, and no CI run to prove against. Tight, ZRLE, TRLE and encrypted authentication (VeNCrypt, TLS, X.509) are not implemented and are refused cleanly, never silently downgraded. VNC Authentication itself is weak by design and must only be used on a trusted network or through an SSH tunnel.

What would unblock it: a controlled Linux VNC server (for example TigerVNC or x11vnc) with documented version, authentication and encodings, a real connection from a device build proving the handshake, authentication and framebuffer updates end to end, and a session screen with scaling, pointer and keyboard input — only then a connect button.
Move hosts between devices with a backup file. Only one format is supported: a TermBridge backup (JSON, version 1). Other files, including PuTTY files, are rejected.

Never exported: trusted host keys (trust must be re-established on first connection after import) and the local folder on this device (a folder choice does not work on another device). Nothing here runs a command or trusts a host key automatically.

Without secrets, the file holds hosts, command buttons, working directories, tunnels, and proxies — but no password, private key, or environment value. After import, credentials and environment values must be entered again.

The passphrase is never stored. If you lose it, the encrypted backup cannot be opened — there is no recovery. It must be at least 8 characters. Anyone with this file can try passphrases offline, without the app\'s protection — use a long, unique passphrase.

Settings that change behaviour arrive with the features they control. For now this screen only leads to diagnostics and about information, and the app follows the system theme.
Screenshots and screen recordings are blocked in this app, so terminal content cannot appear in the Recents overview. This also means you cannot screenshot the app yourself.

TermBridge is an independent app for managing remote servers over SSH. It is not affiliated with any other terminal or remote-access product, and it contains no copied branding, code, or assets from one.

Jetpack Compose (BOM 2024.09.00), Navigation Compose 2.8.0, Kotlin Coroutines 1.8.1, Room 2.6.1, sshj 0.40.0, kotlinx-serialization-json 1.7.3, Material Icons Extended (Compose BOM 2024.09.00), and the AndroidX core, lifecycle, and activity libraries — all Apache License 2.0. Bouncy Castle 1.85 is used under the Bouncy Castle Licence. Test-only dependencies (JUnit, Espresso, Compose UI test) are not shipped in the app.
